description: The access requirement the generated GeneratedRoutePolicy declares per route, as one row per (method, path template) of an entity that declares access (ADR-105). {base} is DomainMetadata.effectivePath(); {id} is the path parameter of one row; {action} is kebab(@Action name), named by the row's action key. entity names the DomainMetadata the row came from. requirement.kind is permitAll, authenticated or anyScope; scopes is present for anyScope only, in declaration order, and the match is any-of. source is entity or action: the declaration the requirement came from, the nearest one winning (an action that declares its own access replaces its entity's; an action that declares none inherits the entity's row). An undeclared route has no row: the generated policy abstains on it and the application's unmatchedRoutes() decides. HEAD is not a row: the policy answers HEAD from the GET rows. Rows follow the router's registration order. RoutePolicyContractE2ETest (exeris-e2e-tests) proves the emitted GeneratedRoutePolicy declares exactly these rows; the codegen-ts guard spec reads the same file. Today the generator extracts no access, so routes is empty; contract/route-policy.example.json shows the row shapes and is checked for shape only. Change this file only together with the policy generator.
